conviction_note: Q3 2026 (9M) is GCP's first report since its 20 Oct ad-hoc on a 20.04% LEG stake. The company itself put that stake at ~30% FFO I accretion, so the one line that could move tomorrow is whether the FY2026 FFO I guide (EUR 175-185m) is raised or the LEG accounting is spelled out. That is an inference. Nothing unpriced and company-level was found, and the stock is already +17% since the stake (+11.9% in 5 days, with Aroundtown and the sector). Hence a small positive findings sum (+0.4) and p_up 52 on a 5% abs move. The scaled +0.2 sits below the sum because the run-up and this name's history of small results-day reactions (|move| <= 2.6% on 8 actual release dates) pull p_up toward 50.

findings.finding: Q3 is the first report since GCP bought 20.04% of LEG, which it said brings >13% FFO I yield and ~30% pro-rata FFO I accretion. If pro-rata LEG FFO counts from 20 Oct (~20% x LEG H1 FFO I EUR 230.5m annualised x ~72 days, less lost interest on ~EUR 0.7bn), FY2026 FFO I lands around EUR 190-195m, above the EUR 175-185m guide, so a guidance raise is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance confirmed with no change on the last three prints: +0.73% (2026-08-12), +0.32% (2026-05-12), -2.55% (2025-11-13). A raise is on record only with H1 2024 ('with increased guidance', https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/grand-city-properties-s-a-announces-h1-2024-results-with-increased-guidance/ca7af9a2-e848-4cf4-8fb3-1964caf038b3_en); that reaction is not measured here. The LEG ad-hoc itself moved the stock +5.62% on 2026-10-21.
findings.why_not_priced: The accretion headline is priced: the stock is +17% since the 20 Oct close (6.76 to 7.92). Whether GCP books pro-rata LEG FFO into its own FFO I and changes the 2026 guide has not been stated. Had the market priced a raise, a broker preview or a German wire piece would name a new FFO figure; none was found. Trading-treff (21 Oct) gives only Aroundtown's +15% and calls it 'noch kein ausgewiesenes Ergebnis'.
findings.independence: Aroundtown's statement of ~15% pro-rata FFO I accretion to the parent (https://trading-treff.de/trading/aroundtown-aktie-leg-investment-hebt-ffo-ausblick) implies the group counts pro-rata LEG FFO. LEG H1 FFO I EUR 230.5m is from paperjam (https://en.paperjam.lu/article/grand-city-properties-is-banking-on-legs-discount). Both rest on the same transaction disclosure.

findings.finding: GCP said it may book a substantial one-off non-cash IFRS profit on the LEG stake: about EUR 1.8bn of attributable LEG book equity against roughly EUR 0.7bn of cost (15.4m shares at ~EUR 46). The Q3 report may quantify or pre-announce it for Q4 and lift the EPRA NTA path. Separately, the stake is up ~EUR 80m at LEG's EUR 51.35.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades at ~30% of EPRA NTA (EUR 7.92 vs EUR 25.8). In 9M 2025 a large non-cash deferred-tax gain (profit EUR 410m) came with a -2.55% day. Non-cash gains have not moved it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed but not quantified, and the accounting route (equity method or fair value) is not stated. It is non-cash, falls in Q4, and is on a 70%-discount-to-NTA stock, so it carries almost no information for the price. Sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Kapitalmarktexperten (10 Nov, German) frames it as 'Buchgewinn ohne Geld' (book gain without cash): https://www.kapitalmarktexperten.de/aroundtown-aktie-buchgewinn-ohne-geld/

findings.finding: The stake used about half of GCP's EUR 1.4bn of cash and liquid assets (31% of debt at June). Berenberg's Kai Klose questioned whether it can be permanent given upcoming refinancing needs, so Q3 liquidity and LTV, and any comment on funding a move to 29.9%, are a live line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No recorded financing-led results day. The H1 2026 perpetual refinancing (5.25% coupon) came with +0.73% on results day.
findings.original_quote: Wegen des anstehenden Refinanzierungsbedarfs hält der Berenberg-Analyst das Investment möglicherweise nicht für dauerhaft. (Translation: because of the upcoming refinancing need, the Berenberg analyst thinks the investment may not be permanent.)
findings.why_not_priced: Asking what the money buys: a >13% FFO yield against GCP's 2.1% average cost of debt (H1) is accretive, so the sign is only mildly negative. It is a public analyst view and partly priced. What Q3 adds is the actual post-deal liquidity figure, which nobody has seen.

findings.finding: Peer read-through: on 2026-10-29 Vonovia cut its 2026 Adj. EBITDA to the lower half and Adj. EBT to the low end, and cut organic rent growth to ~3.8% (from 4%). It cited ~140bp higher unsecured funding costs, a weak transaction market and slower Mietspiegel growth, and gave a first 2027 guide with Adj. EBT roughly flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GCP closed flat on 2026-10-29 (7.10 vs 7.10) when Vonovia fell ~2.5%, and has rallied ~11.5% since. The market did not transmit the peer cut to GCP.
findings.original_quote: Leichte Prognosekorrektur drückt Vonovia-Aktie massiv (headline; translation: a slight forecast correction hits the Vonovia share hard)
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission only, and a hypothesis. GCP's own like-for-like growth was 3.3% at H1 with 95% of debt hedged, so the Vonovia drivers mostly bite in 2027+. Kept small.
